readiness.mainReason: The deck recommends a full supplier migration on a saving it never builds, and a client acting on it could commit the network to a switch that does not pay back.
readiness.highestRiskIssue: Slide 13 recommends the switch while slide 9 leaves the saving behind it unbuilt.
readiness.whatCouldChangeIt: A build for the saving and a fallback in the rollout would change this assessment materially.

findings.title: The deck commits the whole network to a supplier switch on a saving it never builds.
findings.principle: A recommendation carries the weight of its evidence, not more.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 13 states the switch as settled while the saving on slide 9 has no build and no source behind it.

evidence.quote: Client Z should switch to Supplier B.

findings.why: A client that acts on this moves every depot on a number nobody has checked.
findings.reflect: If the saving were half the stated figure, would you still recommend the switch?
findings.fix: Hold the recommendation until the saving is built, or state it conditionally with the threshold that makes it hold.

findings.title: The 2.4 million euro saving is stated with no build and no source.
findings.principle: Evidence grounding: the number a decision turns on carries its own build.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 9 asserts the figure. Nothing shows the unit price delta or the volume it is applied to.

evidence.quote: Switching supplier delivers a 2.4 million euro saving.

findings.why: The whole recommendation turns on this number and the client cannot defend it.
findings.reflect: Write the saving as an equation. Which input is weakest?
findings.fix: Show the build and source each input.

findings.title: The deck names no risk in a switch that moves every depot at once.
findings.principle: An irreversible move states what would make it fail.
findings.diagnosis: The rollout runs from Q1 to Q3 with no risk, no owner and no fallback named anywhere.

evidence.quote: Begin the switch in Q1 and complete migration by Q3.

findings.why: The client has no trigger for stopping if lead times slip.
findings.reflect: What would tell you in month two that this is going wrong?
findings.fix: Add the two or three risks that would stop the switch and what the team would do about each.

questionsForLead: Was the supplier quote behind the saving ever seen by the team, or is it a modelled figure?

learningNote.lesson: An unbuilt number under a recommendation is a decision risk, not a formatting gap.
learningNote.weakHabit: Stating a computed figure as a fact.
learningNote.exercise: Write the headline number as an equation with a source per input.

notAssessed: Slides 6 and 7 are image only in the extract.
